s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic skin eruption with atypical lymphocytic infiltrate
salient_findings: Multiple erythematous and violaceous plaques and nodules on the buttocks
Atypical lymphocytic infiltrate in the dermis with eosinophils and plasma cells
key_facts: Male patient in his 70s
Eruption duration of 5 years
Previous treatments with oral antibiotics, oral doxepin, and UV-B phototherapy failed
History of HSV-2 infection on the buttocks
Syphilis screen results were negative
Molecular analysis of the T-cell receptor gamma gene showed a weak clonal band
Repeat molecular studies showed no evidence of clonal rearrangement
Biopsy findings of dense infiltrate of atypical CD4+ small to medium-sized lymphocytes
Epidermotropism identified in second biopsy
Eosinophils and plasma cells present in the dermal infiltrate

s4.champion: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma

raw.champion: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma
raw.rationale: The presence of a dense infiltrate of atypical CD4+ small to medium-sized lymphocytes in the dermis, along with the clinical presentation of persistent erythematous and violaceous plaques and nodules, supports this diagnosis. The history of HSV-2 infection and failure of previous treatments also aligns with this condition.

rejected.label: Mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: While mycosis fungoides is a type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, the lack of significant epidermotropism in the initial biopsy and the clinical presentation do not strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes several types of lymphomas, but the specific findings in this case point more towards Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not match the typical necrotic and apoptotic features seen in lymphomatoid papulosis.

rejected.label: Cutaneous pseudolymphoma
rejected.why: The presence of atypical lymphocytes and the clinical course suggest a true lymphoma rather than a pseudolymphoma.
